# Pathway Enrichment Analysis

## Setup and Loading Data

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library("tidyverse")
library("broom")
library("msigdbr")

# Read table from 02_clean and fix column types
dat_aug <- read.table("../data/data_aug", header = TRUE, sep = "\t") |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    ENTREZ_ID = as.character(ENTREZ_ID),
    timepoint = as.numeric(timepoint)
  )

dir.create("../results", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Compute Gene-Level log2FC vs Baseline (0h)

Subtract baseline expression from 12h, 24h, 48h and 72h mean expression.

```{r}
#| label: compute-log2fc

#Compute baseline expression per tissue and gene
baseline_0h <- dat_aug |>
  filter(timepoint == 0) |>
  group_by(tissue, ENTREZ_ID) |>
  summarise(expr_0h = mean(expression, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

#Fasting mean expression and subratction
gene_fc <- dat_aug |>
  filter(timepoint > 0) |>
  group_by(tissue, timepoint, ENTREZ_ID) |>
  summarise(expr_t = mean(expression, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(baseline_0h, by = c("tissue", "ENTREZ_ID")) |>
  mutate(log2fc = expr_t - expr_0h)
```

## Hallmark Pathway Enrichment

Hallmark gene sets summarize and represent specific well-defined biological states or processes and display coherent expression. These gene sets were generated by a computational methodology based on identifying overlaps between gene sets in other MSigDB collections and retaining genes that display coordinate expression.

Source: GSEA Website

([https://www.gseamsigdb.org/gsea/msigdb/human/collections.jsp](https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/msigdb/human/collections.jsp)).

Using these predifined biological states helps us group similar pathways into the most important biological processes.

We download the 50 hallmark pathways from mouse and compare with our genes expression change.

```{r}
#| label: pathway-enrichment

# Download the 50 hallmark pathways from mouse
hallmark_mm <- msigdbr(species = "Mus musculus", category = "H") |>
  transmute(
    pathway = gs_name |>
      str_remove("^HALLMARK_") |>
      str_replace_all("_", " ") |>
      str_to_title(),
    ENTREZ_ID = as.character(entrez_gene)
  ) |>
  distinct()

# Enrichment analysis: Tissue, time and pathway (t-test)
#Mean is log2FC = 0, no change in expression
pathway_stats <- gene_fc |>
  inner_join(hallmark_mm, by = "ENTREZ_ID", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  group_by(tissue, timepoint, pathway) |>
  nest() |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    n_genes = map_int(data, nrow),
    test = map(data, ~ tidy(t.test(.x$log2fc, mu = 0)))
  ) |>
  filter(n_genes >= 10) |>
  unnest(test) |>
  group_by(tissue, timepoint) |>
  mutate(
    q_value = p.adjust(p.value, method = "BH"),
    is_sig = q_value < 0.05
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(tissue, timepoint, pathway, n_genes, mean_log2fc = estimate, p.value, q_value, is_sig)

# Save result
write_tsv(pathway_stats, "../results/07_pathway_stats.tsv.gz")
```

## Cross-Organ Pathway Heatmap (72h)

Take the Top20 pathways with expression change and plot a heatmap, comparing the 5 organs (Liver, brain, kidney, instestine, muscle) at 72h fasting.

```{r}
#| label: plot-heatmap
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8

#Select top 20 across with largest change at 72h
top_pathways <- pathway_stats |>
  filter(timepoint == 72, is_sig) |>
  group_by(pathway) |>
  summarise(max_abs_fc = max(abs(mean_log2fc)), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(max_abs_fc, n = 20) |>
  pull(pathway)

#Order pathways by mean log2FC and do heatmap plot
p_heatmap <- pathway_stats |>
  filter(timepoint == 72, pathway %in% top_pathways) |>
  mutate(
    sig_star = if_else(is_sig, "*", ""),
    pathway = fct_reorder(pathway, mean_log2fc, .fun = mean)
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = tissue, y = pathway, fill = mean_log2fc)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = sig_star), size = 4, vjust = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "#2166AC",
    mid = "white",
    high = "#B2182B",
    midpoint = 0,
    name = "Mean log2FC\n(72h vs 0h)"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Top Dysregulated Hallmark Pathways Across Organs at 72h Fasting",
    subtitle = "Asterisks (*) indicate FDR q < 0.05 (one-sample t-test on pathway gene log2FC)",
    x = "Organ",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
  )

p_heatmap

#Save plot
ggsave(
  filename = "../results/07_key_plot_pathways_heatmap.png",
  plot = p_heatmap,
  width = 10,
  height = 8,
  dpi = 300
)
```

-   Most pathwaysare downregulated at 72h, especially immune responses (Interferon Alpha/Gamma, Allograft Rejection) and growth/cell-cycle pathways (mTORC1, G2M Checkpoint). This shows a energy conservation strategy.

-   Muscle shows the strongest overall drop, while liver, and even brain, clearly shut down Cholesterol Homeostasis

-   Intestine is the clear difference, it has mainly an over-expression behaviour (more red). It is the only organ upregulating lipid and detox pathways (Fatty Acid, Bile Acid, Peroxisome, Xenobiotic Metabolism) at 72h.

## Pathways change over fasting time (Top 6)

Get the 6 pathways that have changes the most and see how they evolved from 12h to 72 in the 5 organs. This way we can see where do they activate/deactivate.

```{r}
#| label: plot-kinetics
#| echo: true
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 11

#Select top6
top6_pathways <- pathway_stats |>
  filter(is_sig) |>
  group_by(pathway) |>
  summarise(max_abs_fc = max(abs(mean_log2fc)), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(max_abs_fc, n = 6) |>
  pull(pathway)

# Add 0h baseline (log2FC = 0) so curves start from zero
kinetics_df <- pathway_stats |>
    filter(pathway %in% top6_pathways)

baseline_points <- kinetics_df |>
    distinct(tissue, pathway) |>
    mutate(timepoint = 0, mean_log2fc = 0, is_sig = FALSE)

#Plot trajectory over fasting hours
#Filled dot means significant (FDR < 0.05)
p_kinetics <- bind_rows(baseline_points, kinetics_df) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = timepoint, y = mean_log2fc, color = tissue)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
    geom_point(aes(shape = is_sig), size = 2.5) +
    scale_shape_manual(
        values = c("FALSE" = 1, "TRUE" = 16),
        name = "FDR q < 0.05"
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 12, 24, 48, 72)) +
    facet_wrap(~ pathway, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(
        title = "Temporal Dynamics of Top Fasting-Regulated Pathways Across Organs",
        x = "Fasting Duration (hours)",
        y = "Mean Pathway log2FC (vs. 0h)",
        color = "Organ"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11)

p_kinetics

#Save plot
ggsave(
  filename = "../results/07_pathways_kinetics.png",
  plot = p_kinetics,
  width = 11,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```

-   Muscle reacts fastest and hardest, dropping sharply within the first 12h across almost all top pathways.

-   Most organs follow the same pattern. First they drop (0-24h), then they usually stabilize or increase (24-48h) and finally, when fasting is at a long stage (72h), they decrease considerably again.

-   Fatty Acid Metabolism rises early in kidney, liver, and intestine (12–48h) before falling back in liver and kidney at 72h, while liver Cholesterol Homeostasis drops steadily from start to finish.
